title: Redwood POC weekly sync - benchmark review vs baseline provider
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs the customer's baseline provider. Redwood showed improved p95/p99 latency and higher token throughput at target batch sizes after batching/KV-cache tuning. Customer concerned about 8k context p99 spikes and consistency vs baseline; asked for private cluster run and full trace. Agreed next steps: run private 8k latency tests, share updated spreadsheet and config snippets, schedule infra deep-dive next week.
action_items: Ethan Wu - run p50/p95/p99 latency tests on Redwood private cluster for 4k and 8k contexts, include warm/cold KV cache runs - due 2026-04-03
Maya Rodriguez - share sample workload trace and peak QPS spreadsheet - due 2026-04-01
Sofia Patel - send updated benchmark spreadsheet with raw logs and config used (batch sizes, quant profile) - due 2026-03-31
Kenji Tanaka - validate accuracy/regression on quantized 4-bit model against baseline testset and report any mismatches - due 2026-04-06
Jamal Ortiz - prepare short infra deep-dive agenda and invite list for 2026-04-08 meeting
next_steps: Redwood to run private-cluster 8k context tests and share results
Customer to provide production traffic trace and top prompt templates
Schedule infra deep-dive (networking, VPC, HSM) next Thursday
Sofia to follow up with pricing delta for Dedicated vs Hosted for pilot scale
transcript:
Date: 2026-03-30 | Time: 15:00 PDT | Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Wu (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Redwood CSM), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SRE); Maya Rodriguez (Astra CTO), Kenji Tanaka (Astra ML), Priya Singh (Astra Infra), Liam O'Connor (Astra SRE)

Summary: quick recap of last week's runs, dug into p95/p99 spikes at high context, talked tuning knobs (batch size, kv cache warm paths), customer asked for private-run results and artifacts.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we'll keep this to 40 minutes. quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya: Maya here.
[00:09] Kenji: Kenji.
[00:11] Priya: Priya.
[00:12] Liam: Liam.
[00:14] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood.
[00:15] Lena: Lena here.
[00:17] Jamal: Jamal.
[00:20] Sofia: Great. Agenda for today - benchmark review vs your baseline provider, discuss the 8k context p99 spikes, go over tuning we did, and agree next steps. Ethan do you want to start with the numbers?
[00:31] Ethan: Yep. So we re-ran the set with the same sample prompts you shared, matched the qps pattern - 200 concurrent users, peak bursts to 500, and two sequence lengths: 2k and 8k. For 2k context our p50 was ~45ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~170ms. Baseline provider numbers we have from your spreadsheet were p50 55ms, p95 230ms, p99 320ms so we see consistent improvement. Throughput at steady-state tokens/sec was about 18k tps for us vs baseline ~11k, measured at target batch size of 32.
[01:05] Kenji: those numbers look good, but we noticed the 8k runs had p99 spikes - can you explain the cause?
[01:12] Ethan: yeah so 8k has two effects: kernel dispatch overhead for long attention, and KV-cache warm ups. In some cold-start cases we observed large p99s up to 1.2s. after we tuned continuous batching and increased the prefetch for KV cache warm path those spikes reduced to ~420ms p99 in our private-run. but note some of the variance is due to your prompt distribution - long generation tails are more sensitive.
[01:40] Maya: The baseline provider p99 for 8k in our tests was around 600-700ms, so you're still better on average but the variance is concerning for SLA.
[01:49] Ethan: totally, which is why we recommend two levers: first, set the soft SLO to route high-priority traffic to Dedicated nodes (lower queue times), second, enable prefix caching for repeated prompts - that removed 30-40% of tokens per request in our traces.
[02:06] Priya: quick question - when you say prefix caching is it per-tenant KV or global? rolling privacy implications?
[02:14] Ethan: it's per-tenant in the POC setup. we store the encoded KV (not raw text) and you can set retention/eviction policies; for Private/VPC you control keys via KMS. apologies if earlier notes said KV cash, not cache, there is some transcriber mis-typo in the doc.
[02:32] Liam: on the infra side, network egress and cross-AZ hops might add 20-40ms during spikes; did you simulate cross-az traffic?
[02:40] Jamal: we did some multi-az tests; in the hosted runs there's a tail added by cross-az routing, but on Dedicated/Priate (private) cluster we colocated and that went away.
[02:51] Kenji: can you share config? batch sizes, quant, gpus used?
[02:55] Ethan: sure: for the runs we used a 8x A100 equivalent Dedicated pool for 8k tests, model quantized to 4-bit with our PQAT profile - we also tried 3-bit for throughput-only runs but saw quality drop of ~1.8% on your eval set. batch sizes: 32 for steady state, 8 for cold/low qps. we turned on continuous batching window at 12ms. I'll attach the exact config in the spreadsheet.
[03:25] Maya: that quant drop is acceptable for many internal flows but not for billing/clinical text. Kenji will run the regression test.
[03:33] Kenji: yeah I'll run it. also curious about cost - how does your per-token cost compare to baseline when you factor Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:41] Sofia: quick take - at pilot scale (50k tokens/day) Hosted is cheaper to start, Dedicated gives better unit cost at committed throughput. We'll send a delta pricing calc.
[03:52] Priya: Another ask - can you run the same 8k context tests on our private cluster (air-gapped-ish) or at least in our VPC? we want to see exact network effect and GPU SKU parity.
[04:02] Ethan: yes we can run on your VPC. we have a remote runner for your env; need get access to an AMI and VPN, and Maya to provide service account. For air-gapped on-prem there are extra steps but doable.
[04:16] Sofia: For visibility, we've added token-level breakdowns and traces to the spreadsheet - the raw logs include timestamps and kernel-level timing.
[04:24] Kenji: perfect. one more: the p99 spikes - are they reproducible on-demand or intermittent?
[04:29] Ethan: mostly intermittent tied to cold KV and large generation tails; we can reproduce by clearing cache and firing a cold surge pattern like you had in traces. small crosstalk: (Priya) "so is this the KV cache vs KMS again?"
[04:46] Priya: yeah I misheard earlier.
[04:47] Ethan: no worries. if we pre-warm cache for high-pri traffic we see p99 shrink significantly.
[04:52] Maya: ok let's be explicit: we want a run on your private cluster for 8k, include both warm and cold cache profiles, and capture p50/p95/p99 and raw trace.
[04:59] Sofia: noted. Ethan can you call out the exact set you'll run?
[05:04] Ethan: we'll run four experiments: (1) cold-cache 8k 200qps burst profile, (2) warm-cache 8k steady 200qps, (3) warm-cache with increased batch size 48 to see throughput scaling, (4) 4k baseline runs for comparison. We'll produce CSVs and kernel timing logs.
[05:20] Kenji: also please include model version and exact quant bits in the CSV.
[05:24] Ethan: yes, model v2.1.3-quant4b and v2.1.3-quant3b where applicable.
[05:29] Maya: any blockers on our side?
[05:32] Priya: we'll need to get you the service account and VPC access. timing wise we can grant that by Friday.
[05:38] Sofia: great. quick note on security/compliance - we discussed KMS/HSM and audit logs last week; customer asked for SOC2 box and SAML SSO detail. we'll include the SOC2 addendum in the follow up.
[05:50] Lena: i'll attach the security pack and the SOC2 link in the follow up email.
[05:53] Maya: thanks.
[05:55] Ethan: one last thing on throughput - on the provider baseline we observed their batching window set to 25ms, we run 12ms so lower queuing but more frequent kernel calls; that's part of why throughput improved while lowering p95. there's a tradeoff depending on your acceptable latency curve.
[06:15] Kenji: ok makes sense.
[06:17] Sofia: recap/nx steps? quick bullets: Sofia to send spreadsheet and pricing, Ethan to run private 8k experiments and share logs, Maya to provide service account and traces, Kenji to run quant accuracy checks, Jamal to schedule infra deep-dive.
[06:33] Maya: sounds good.
[06:35] Liam: thanks all.
[06:36] Sofia: we'll follow up with links and calendar invite for deep-dive. Thanks everyone.
